text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This keeps quality high by catching obvious fixes fast while avoiding bottlenecks. The trade-off is risk—some changes might break edge cases—but the "safe" filter limits exposure.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t edge cases—it’s that "safe" is subjective until proven by failure. A typo fix might mask a logic error in routing; formatting might hide a prompt that’s brittle under load. A better alternative: auto-apply only changes with a pre-approved regression test, then log the rest. Settle it with a pilot—run the filter for a week, measure breakage, and decide if the risk is worth the speed.

name: Overhaul
text: Auto-apply only changes that pass a static analysis check (e.g., linting for syntax errors) and a smoke test (e.g., a minimal prompt run) before logging the rest. This shifts the "safe" filter from human judgment to automated proof, cutting review load while reducing hidden risk.

This removes human guesswork from "safe" and replaces it with automated proof, cutting hidden risks like brittle prompts or routing errors. The trade-off is slower initial rollouts for edge cases, but the reduction in post-deployment fixes justifies it.
